source_title: 40 more farm fire cases in Punjab; FIR count at 246 - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Bathinda: Punjab accounted for 40 of the 44 stubble-burning cases reported across states on Friday. The remaining four cases were reported from Rajasthan, taking the total number of farm fire incidents to 2,739 across seven states. Punjab had recorded 194 farm fire cases on Thursday, the highest single-day count of the ongoing paddy harvesting season.Tarn Taran continued to top the chart among the 159 districts across seven states that have reported stubble burning so far, with 405 cases. Amritsar ranked fourth with 175 cases, behind Rajasthanâs Baran (194) and Bundi (192) districts.Of the total farm fire cases recorded so far, Punjab has reported 1,047, followed by Rajasthan (614), Madhya Pradesh (528), Uttar Pradesh (345), Uttarakhand (174), Haryana (29) and Delhi (2).With the spike in farm fire incidents, punitive action has also intensified. A total of 246 FIRs have been registered under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for disobedience of orders duly promulgated by a public servant. These include 165 FIRs in Tarn Taran, 24 in Amritsar, 17 in Kapurthala, 10 each in Ferozepur and Jalandhar, seven in Gurdaspur, four each in Fazilka and Patiala, two each in Muktsar and Sangrur, and one in Faridkot.Environmental compensation (EC) of Rs 17.5 lakh has been imposed in 349 cases, of which Rs 13.15 lakh has been recovered.Red entries have been made in land records in 297 cases, including 177 in Tarn Taran, 58 in Amritsar, 17 in Kapurthala, 10 each in Ferozepur and Jalandhar, seven in Gurdaspur, five in Fatehgarh Sahib, four in Fazilka, two each in Muktsar and Sangrur, and one each in Barnala, Bathinda, Faridkot, Hoshiarpur and Patiala.The authorities have also issued warning and show-cause notices to 426 nodal and supervisory officers.According to the Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modelling from Space (CREAMS), stubble burning incidents have so far been reported from 159 districts, including 22 districts in Punjab.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
